goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:48 — Deferring cancellation until a cron run inside the final hour lets a cancellation made after the last cron tick miss the deadline and deliver the reminder anyway.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real race condition in the new cancellation logic. Looking at scheduleEmailReminders.ts lines 43-75, cancelled reminders are only processed if their scheduledDate is within the next hour (`lte: dayjs().add(1, 'hour').toISOString()`). If a booking is cancelled after the last cron run but before the scheduled reminder time (which could be less than an hour away), the cancellation won't be processed in time and the reminder will still be sent. The cron job only cancels reminders scheduled within the next hour, so a cancellation made between cron runs could miss the window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — The unbounded global scan followed by serial SendGrid calls lets one tenant create enough cancelled reminders to time out the worker and starve cancellations for every tenant.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that scheduleEmailReminders.ts performs an unbounded query for all cancelled reminders within the next hour (no limit clause), then iterates through them serially making individual SendGrid API calls. This is a real scalability/DoS concern - if many reminders are cancelled, the worker could timeout. The code at lines 44-75 shows: findMany without limit, then a for loop making sequential client.request calls. This is a legitimate performance/reliability bug that could affect all tenants.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53 — One poisoned SendGrid batch aborts all later cancellations while the catch still permits an HTTP 200 response, so retries and monitoring can silently pass as due reminders are sent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a for-loop at lines 53-70 in scheduleEmailReminders.ts that iterates through remindersToCancel and makes SendGrid API calls. If any single client.request() call fails, the catch block at line 72 only logs the error and continues, allowing the HTTP 200 response. This means: 1) Later reminders in the loop won't be processed if an early one fails (the loop is inside the try block), 2) The workflowRemindersToDelete array won't be fully populated, 3) The function returns success despite partial failure. This is a real bug where a single poisoned batch_id could abort processing of subsequent cancellations while the endpoint reports success.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — One SendGrid cancellation failure aborts the whole loop and skips its queued database deletions, allowing later cancelled reminders to be sent.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in scheduleEmailReminders.ts lines 52-75, the code iterates through remindersToCancel in a for loop, making SendGrid API calls and queuing database deletions. The entire loop is wrapped in a single try-catch block. If any SendGrid request fails (e.g., for the first reminder), the catch block is triggered and execution jumps to the error handler, skipping all subsequent reminders in the loop. The workflowRemindersToDelete array would not be fully populated, and Promise.all would only delete reminders processed before the failure. This means cancelled reminders that weren't processed would remain in the database without being cancelled in SendGrid, potentially causing them to be sent.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:488 — The reschedule mutation no longer awaits reminder cleanup, so it can return success before old email or SMS reminders are cancelled.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx, the old code had `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete);` after collecting reminder deletion promises. The new code removes this await and the Promise.all entirely - it just calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder in a forEach loop without awaiting. Looking at deleteScheduledEmailReminder in emailReminderManager.ts, it's an async function that makes database calls. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:376 — Disabling event types now discards the reminder-manager promises, so the workflow update can finish while removed-event reminders are still active.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx around line 372-386, the old code had `deleteReminderPromise` array that collected promises and then awaited them with `await Promise.all(deleteReminderPromise)`. The new code removes this Promise.all and just calls the delete functions in a forEach loop without awaiting them. The deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder functions are async (as seen in their implementations in the diff), so calling them without await means the workflow update can complete while the reminder cancellations are still in progress. This is a fire-and-forget pattern that could leave reminders active if the cancellation fails or takes time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:197 — The new cancellation API leaks database ids, provider references, and an ambiguous boolean mode into every caller; replace it with one reminder-level lifecycle operation.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the new deleteScheduledEmailReminder function signature (reminderId: number, referenceId: string | null, immediateDelete?: boolean) exposes internal implementation details to callers. Looking at the diff, this function is called from multiple places (handleCancelBooking.ts, handleNewBooking.ts, bookings.tsx, workflows.tsx) with varying parameters. The boolean 'immediateDelete' parameter creates an ambiguous API where callers must understand internal scheduling behavior. This is a legitimate architectural/design concern about API design, not a bug, but it's grounded in specific code changes in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:57 — The cron duplicates the SendGrid cancellation request implemented by deleteScheduledEmailReminder, so provider changes require synchronized edits; route both paths through one provider adapter.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the diff introduces duplicate SendGrid cancellation logic. In scheduleEmailReminders.ts lines 57-66, there's a direct SendGrid API call to cancel scheduled sends. Meanwhile, deleteScheduledEmailReminder in emailReminderManager.ts also contains SendGrid cancellation logic (when immediateDelete is true). This is a valid architectural concern - having the same provider-specific logic in two places means changes to the SendGrid API would require synchronized edits in both locations. This is a legitimate maintainability/architecture concern grounded in the actual diff, though not a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:54 — The handler names Prisma's generated internal Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient type just to batch deletes, creating a brittle generated-client dependency; use inferred promises or deleteMany.

adjudication.rationale: The diff at line 54 shows `const workflowRemindersToDelete: Prisma.Prisma__WorkflowReminderClient<WorkflowReminder, never>[] = [];` which does use Prisma's internal generated client type. This is a valid architectural concern - using internal Prisma types creates coupling to generated code that could change. The suggestion to use inferred types or deleteMany is reasonable. However, this is not a bug - the code will work correctly, it's just a maintainability/coupling concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:2 — Combining the imports converts App, Credential, EventTypeCustomInput, and Prisma from type-only dependencies into value imports just to add WorkflowMethods; retain a separate import type boundary.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that combining imports converts type-only imports to value imports. However, looking at the diff, the original code shows 'import type { App, Credential, EventTypeCustomInput, Prisma }' which are type imports, and the new code imports them as values. But in TypeScript/JavaScript, importing types as values when they are only used as types is handled by the compiler and doesn't cause runtime issues. Additionally, WorkflowMethods is used as a value (WorkflowMethods.EMAIL, WorkflowMethods.SMS) so it needs to be a value import. The other imports (App, Credential, EventTypeCustomInput, Prisma) may or may not be used as values elsewhere in the file - we can't determine this from the diff alone. This is at most a minor style preference, not a real issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:2 — PrismaPromise is used only as a type while Prisma is entirely unused, but both were added to the value import; remove Prisma and restore a type-only import.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx, the change shows PrismaPromise being moved from a type import to a value import, and Prisma is also imported. However, examining the full diff context, Prisma is actually used in the file - for example, 'Prisma.BatchPayload' type references would require the Prisma import. adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44 — The cron materializes every due cancelled reminder and performs one serial SendGrid request per row, so a backlog can exhaust memory or the execution window; process bounded pages instead.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that scheduleEmailReminders.ts fetches all cancelled reminders with `findMany` without any limit/pagination, then iterates through them serially making SendGrid API calls. This is a valid architectural concern - if there's a large backlog of cancelled reminders, this could cause memory issues or timeout the cron job. However, this is not a bug per se (the code will work correctly for normal loads), but rather a scalability/performance concern that a reasonable reviewer might flag. The finding correctly identifies the unbounded query and serial processing pattern in the new code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/prisma/migrations/20230217230604_add_cancelled_to_workflow_reminder/migration.sql:2 — The new cancelled-by-scheduledDate cron lookup has no supporting index and therefore scans WorkflowReminder on every run; add a composite or partial index for this predicate.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new query in scheduleEmailReminders.ts that filters WorkflowReminder by 'cancelled: true' and 'scheduledDate: { lte: ... }'. The migration only adds the 'cancelled' column without any index. This is a valid performance concern - the cron job will scan the entire WorkflowReminder table on every run. While not a bug (it will work correctly), it's a legitimate architectural concern for a table that could grow large. The finding correctly identifies the specific code location and the missing index.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53 — One SendGrid cancellation failure aborts the entire cancellation loop while the endpoint still returns success, allowing every later due reminder to be sent.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in scheduleEmailReminders.ts lines 53-79, the code iterates through remindersToCancel with a for loop, making await calls to client.request() for each reminder. If any single SendGrid API call fails, the catch block at line 80 only logs the error ('Error cancelling scheduled Emails') but doesn't prevent the endpoint from continuing and returning success. This means: 1) If one cancellation fails mid-loop, subsequent reminders in the loop won't be processed (the loop breaks on error), 2) The workflowRemindersToDelete array won't be fully populated, 3) The endpoint still proceeds to process unscheduledReminders and returns success. This allows reminders that should have been cancelled to still be sent, which is a real bug in the cancellation logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:213 — The immediate-delete branch swallows SendGrid failures without marking the reminder cancelled, leaving failed reschedule cancellations outside the cron retry set.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for emailReminderManager.ts lines 206-222, the `immediateDelete` branch (lines 213-222) calls the SendGrid API to cancel the scheduled send, but if this API call fails, the error is caught in the outer catch block at line 231 which only logs the error. The reminder is never marked as cancelled or deleted, and since `immediateDelete` returns early (line 221), the reminder won't be picked up by the cron job's retry mechanism (which looks for `cancelled: true` reminders). This is a real bug where failed immediate cancellations are silently lost.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:485 — The nested forEach discards reminder-cancellation promises, so the handler can report success and terminate before cancellation state or SMS deletion is persisted.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in handleCancelBooking.ts, the code iterates through reminders with forEach and calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder. These functions are async (as seen in emailReminderManager.ts and smsReminderManager.ts where they perform prisma operations and API calls), but the forEach doesn't await them. The old code collected PrismaPromises into remindersToDelete array and included them in prismaPromises for Promise.all. The new code removes this - the remindersToDelete array and its inclusion in prismaPromises are deleted. So the async cancellation operations are fire-and-forget, meaning the handler can complete before the database updates (setting cancelled=true or deleting reminders) are persisted.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966 — Rescheduling fire-and-forgets all old-reminder cancellations, so a request ending after the new booking succeeds can leave the old notifications scheduled.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at lines 964-977 in handleNewBooking.ts that workflow reminder cancellations are called inside a try-catch block but without awaiting them. The forEach loop calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder which are async functions, but they're not awaited. This means the cancellation requests are fire-and-forget - the code continues to create the new booking while the old reminder cancellations may still be in progress or may fail silently. If the request ends or fails after the new booking succeeds, the old notifications could remain scheduled. This is a real concurrency/race condition bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:488 — This reschedule mutation no longer awaits reminder deletion or cancellation, so it can complete with the previous booking's notifications still active.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx, the old code had `await Promise.all(remindersToDelete);` after collecting all reminder deletion promises. The new code removes this await and the Promise.all entirely - it just calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder in a forEach loop without awaiting them. Looking at the implementations in emailReminderManager.ts and smsReminderManager.ts, these are async functions that perform database operations. Without awaiting, the reschedule mutation can complete before the reminders are actually cancelled/deleted, potentially leaving stale reminders active.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:376 — Disabling event types launches reminder mutations without awaiting them, replacing the prior awaited deletion with background work that may be dropped at request completion.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff around line 376 in workflows.tsx, the code changes from using `await Promise.all(deleteReminderPromise)` to calling `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` in a forEach loop without awaiting. The old code collected promises and awaited them all. The new code in the forEach just calls the async functions without await, meaning these operations run in the background and may not complete before the request ends. This is a real defect - the reminder deletions/cancellations may be dropped.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleEmailReminders.ts:34 — No boundary test covers a cancelled reminder whose scheduled time has passed, so cleanup can delete its row before SendGrid receives cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a potential race condition in the new cancellation logic at scheduleEmailReminders.ts lines 42-77. The code queries for reminders with `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate <= now + 1 hour`, then sends a cancel request to SendGrid, then deletes the database row. If a reminder's scheduled time has already passed (but is still within the 1-hour window), the row could be deleted before SendGrid processes the cancellation, or the SendGrid cancellation might fail for an already-sent email. This is a legitimate edge case concern about the new workflow cancellation logic, though it's more of an incomplete edge-case handling than a definite bug. The finding correctly identifies that no boundary test covers this scenario.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:485 — No lifecycle test asserts reminder cancellation finishes before the handler returns, leaving the newly unawaited email and SMS operations able to be dropped.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in handleCancelBooking.ts, the workflow reminder deletion calls (deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder) are now called inside forEach loops without awaiting them, and they're no longer added to the prismaPromises array that gets awaited. This means these async operations could be dropped if the handler returns before they complete.
